_doc: #881 Jev wave 0: THE ONE DECLARATION of the fleet's decisions engine (libs:decisions-engine, Cloud-Lib-Decisions-Engine.apk), baked into that APK as an asset and read by that engine only. It lives beside the engine, not in fleet-config.json: that manifest is baked into the SuperApp and every app, so tuning a threshold there would ship the SuperApp and refresh 33 apps, while here a wave's new use rebuilds one lib APK. The engine's state (the ledger, the answer cache, consent and the journal) is in its filesDir/decisions/, per phone by design, so a new phone starts at the declared defaults. Jev is TypeSafe's decision model on OpenRouter's Decisions API: it scores options the caller already has and never generates or computes. The engine holds the OpenRouter token in its own process (read from the Account vault through text-tools, never across the binder) and answers `decide(use, state, questions)` for apps that hold no key. A Jev answer only reorders, pre-selects or suggests; every refusal or failure is {ok:false, reason} and the caller keeps today's behaviour; a site's static deny list runs before it calls. `uses` is the same shape the host gate declares in _shared/jev-gate/jev-gate.json::uses (enabled, threshold, allowed, class, ttl_s, max_calls_per_hour) plus `apps` (the packages allowed to call it; the engine reads the caller from the binder), `consent` and `content`. class: user_facing may pre-select or re-rank; background must declare ttl_s (cached, never re-asked); gating answers advice_only. consent: required = off until the user grants it to the app (any use whose content is in sensitive_content is required, whatever it says); implicit = on. Only the apps in consent_setters may record a grant. `allowed` closes the option keys a choice question of the use may offer. budget: the fleet's daily USD cap (UTC day), a per-app daily call quota and est_call_usd charged when an answer carries no usage.cost. suppress: nothing is sent while offline, on a metered network or in battery saver (cached answers are still served). breaker: after `failures` consecutive failures nothing is sent for open_s seconds, then one trial. redact: drop_keys are removed from the state, the value of a key matching secret_key is masked, every string goes through patterns (Java regex, replacement `$1` = group 1), and a state over max_chars is refused, never truncated. A new use lands with its wave (#882 advisory, #883 user-facing, #884 gating) declared here, and the decisions-use guard fails the build when a decide(use) call names one that is not.

probe._doc: #881 wave 0: the plumbing's own end-to-end check, called only by the engine's /api/decisions/probe debug route (so only on a debug build) to prove token, endpoint, budget and cache work. Its question is a fixed arithmetic statement; no user data is in it. Waves #882-#884 declare their uses beside it.
